newsitem.title: USA: Microsoft leads tech decline, pushing Nasdaq lower.
newsitem.headline: Microsoft leads tech decline, pushing Nasdaq lower.

text.p: News that Microsoft Corp may delay the successor to its Windows 95 operating system pressured the already weak technology sector on Monday, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index dropped 11.43 points or 0.91 percent to close unofficially at 1242.64. The Nasdaq's declined sharply contrasted with the Dow industrials, which gained 100 points to 6905.
"There's just a black cloud that has settled over the techs lately and any bit of news makes the sector react violently. There's tremendous sensitivity," one trader said.

Microsoft led the technology sell-off, falling 3-7/8 to 90-1/8. Cisco Systems Inc shed 2-1/8 to 47-1/8 and Novellus Systems Inc dropped 3-1/4 to 65-3/4. But Intel Corp showed slight gains after the company said it remained on track to meet its aggressive new product plans.
In other news, shares of Medic Computer System Inc, IDEXX Laboratories Inc and Sonic Corp crumbled after each company warned investors its quartely results would fall short of Wall Street estimates.
Overall, declining issues beat gainers 2604 to 1658 on total volume of 610 million shares.
